mainEntity.name: Is MCPEmails an IMAP MCP server?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Alongside Gmail and Outlook there is a generic IMAP and SMTP connector, so any mailbox with IMAP access works: your own domain, a hosting provider, a regional ISP. You enter the server details and an app password once, and your agent reads over IMAP and sends through your own SMTP server.

mainEntity.name: Can one agent work several mailboxes at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Connect each mailbox to the same account and your agent reaches all of them through one endpoint. It can list the connected inboxes, pick the right one for each request, and move between, say, a support address and a personal one in the same conversation. How many inboxes you can connect depends on your plan.

mainEntity.name: How do I add the email MCP connector to Claude or ChatGPT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add a custom connector in your client settings, paste https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp as the server URL, and approve the sign-in. Clients that support OAuth need no API key. The same URL works in Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients.
We use privacy-preserving, cookieless product analytics to understand site and setup performance. We never collect email content, addresses, API keys, OAuth tokens, or MCP request data.

mainEntity.name: Which AI clients does it work with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any MCP-compatible client. We're a standard streamable-http MCP server with OAuth 2.1, DCR and PKCE, so the same inbox works in Claude, Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT, Windsurf, n8n, Make, LibreChat and more. Paste one endpoint URL and you're connected, with no per-app rebuild.

mainEntity.name: Which email providers can I connect?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gmail and Google Workspace with a Google app password over IMAP, Outlook and Microsoft 365 by signing in with Microsoft (a work or school account may need its IT admin to approve the app once), Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho and Yandex with an app-specific password, and any other mailbox over a generic IMAP/SMTP connection. Connect as many inboxes as you like and label them by use case.

No. The mail your agent reads is fetched live from your provider on each request and never stored on our servers. The exceptions are outgoing messages that have to wait: a message you schedule for later, or a send held for your approval, is stored encrypted.

Yes. The free plan connects one inbox, forever, with no card required, and your agent can read, search, send, reply, schedule and organise in it. Personal is $9 a month for a second and third mailbox on the same agent, Pro covers up to 10 for $15, and Business is for more mailboxes or when other people need in.

mainEntity.name: What can the AI actually do with my inbox?

acceptedAnswer.text: Read and search mail, send, reply and forward real messages, schedule sends for later, and organize your inbox: move, copy, flag, archive and delete. Twenty-one action-based tools, so the agent finishes the job inside your inbox instead of just drafting.

mainEntity.name: How do I connect an inbox?

acceptedAnswer.text: Create a free account, connect your mailbox (a Google app password for Gmail, sign in with Microsoft for Outlook, or paste an app password for the others), then drop https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp into your AI client and authorize. Your agent has the inbox in a couple of minutes.

Yes. MCPEmails is open source under AGPL-3.0, and the hosted service runs the same server you can run yourself. A docker-compose stack gets the full MCP server and all its tools running against your own database in about five minutes, for any IMAP or SMTP mailbox. Gmail and Outlook sign-in (OAuth) and the dashboard stay on the hosted plan.
